feedback:
Judged from earlier races and this candidate's contents only. Nothing here states how the candidate will perform.

The candidate is a single-variable step from the best raced design (iteration 4, score 238.08). Only kd changes, from 0.55 to 0.60. Geometry (sensor_size 0.012, x = ±0.04), kp 4.0, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.5, weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2) and last_direction are held, so any race difference can be attributed to kd. The values are inside the contract limits.

Evidence: kd 0.2 to 0.4 gave +101, 0.4 to 0.5 gave +6 (iteration 3), and 0.5 to 0.55 gave +62 (iteration 4). Oval steering_oscillation was 0.298 at kd 0.5 and 0.297 at kd 0.55, so it has not been rising with kd. The 0.32 revert threshold still has margin. The sensor-footprint branch is closed: sensor_size 0.016 scored 157.9 in iteration 6, so it should not be retried. Widening the span to ±0.06 in iteration 5 cut line losses (s-bend 1.00 to 0.25) but dropped the score to 219.9 by reducing oval finishes from 8 to 7. Lowering base_speed to 1.3 (iteration 2) cut the score to 86.8, so speed is not the lever.

What to do with the next race:
- If the score beats 238 and oval steering_oscillation stays under about 0.32, keep kd 0.6. The remaining line losses (about 1.0 on the s-bend and slalom) then point to sensing, so test an intermediate span of about ±0.05 (weights unchanged) next, since ±0.06 cut losses but cost finishes.
- If the score falls below 238, or steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.32, revert to kd 0.55 (the iteration 4 design). Do not raise kd further, and test the ±0.05 span at kd 0.55 instead.

Report per-track line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation, plus oval completion and completion_time, so the damping effect can be separated from the sensing effect.
